$meta.title: Caribbean Sea-Level-Rise Risk Scores — Coastal Jurisdictions
sources: NOAA Climate.gov — https://www.climate.gov/ (state of the climate)
Climate Central — https://www.climatecentral.org/ (coastal risk screening tool)
Caribbean Community Climate Change Centre (CCCCC) — https://www.caribbeanclimate.bz/
IPCC AR6 WG1 Chapter 9 (Ocean, cryosphere, sea-level change)
caveats: ALL risk scores in this file are APPROXIMATED from publicly available regional summaries and IPCC AR6 WG1 regional projections.
Every numeric value carries `unverified: true` UNLESS a specific dataset URL is cited in the record's `sourceDataset` field.
These scores are screening-level indicators only — they DO NOT replace a licensed surveyor, an insurer's valuation, or an official flood map.
Local variation within a jurisdiction can be orders of magnitude greater than the national average (e.g. the south coast of Barbados vs. the west coast).
Climate models diverge substantially by 2100; this file uses the IPCC AR6 SSP2-4.5 'intermediate' scenario as the central case.

scoringScale.0: Negligible — <10% of coastline exposed to 1m SLR by 2100

BS.regionalContext: Low-lying carbonate archipelago; ~80% of land within 1m of mean sea level. Hurricane Dorian (2019) demonstrated catastrophic storm-surge vulnerability.
BS.sourceDataset: IPCC AR6 WG1 Figure 9.27 (Caribbean region SSP2-4.5); Climate Central CoastalDEM 2022
BS.leaseholderImplication: Many Bahamian leaseholds (condominiums on New Providence / Paradise Island) are within 50m of high-tide line; service charges for insurance + remediation should be audited annually.

BB.regionalContext: Single coral island, ~430 km², southernmost Caribbean. South coast (Christ Church, St. Philip) is flat and exposed; west coast (St. James, St. Peter) is limestone cliff-backed.
BB.sourceDataset: CCCCC Caribbean Climate Change Profile (Barbados); IPCC AR6 WG1 Caribbean region
BB.leaseholderImplication: Condominiums on the south coast (e.g. Rockley, Worthing) carry measurable insurance premium escalation risk. Leaseholders should verify that the strata insurance policy has a flood sub-limit and a climate-change exclusion review clause.

JM.regionalContext: Mountainous island (~2,200m peaks) with narrow coastal plains. Kingston waterfront and Port Antonio are the most exposed. Hurricane Irma/Maria (2017) demonstrated surge vulnerability on the north coast.
JM.sourceDataset: Climate Studies Division, Mona (UWI) — Caribbean Climate Change Profile (Jamaica); IPCC AR6 WG1
JM.leaseholderImplication: Kingston harbour condominiums + Port Antonio villas carry the highest risk. Strata insurance for Montego Bay should be reviewed for flood sub-limits; inland St. Andrew properties are largely unaffected.

KY.regionalContext: Low-lying limestone islands; Seven Mile Beach (Grand Cayman) is the tourism + luxury-condo centre and lies <2m above MSL for most of its length.
KY.sourceDataset: Cayman Islands National Climate Change Office (NCCO); Climate Central CoastalDEM 2022
KY.leaseholderImplication: Seven Mile Beach strata-titled condominiums (the bulk of Caymanian leasehold value) carry severe risk by 2100 under SSP2-4.5. FreeLeased recommends leaseholders in KY verify the strata insurance has a 100-year flood return-period endorsement and a 1m SLR exclusion review by 2030.

TT.regionalContext: Two main islands; Trinidad is mountainous with narrow coastal plains; Tobago has flatter south-coast (Crown Point, Store Bay) that is tourism-critical and low-elevation.
TT.sourceDataset: Trinidad & Tobago Meteorological Service — Caribbean Climate Change Profile
TT.leaseholderImplication: Tobago south-coast condominiums (Crown Point area) carry meaningful risk; Trinidad's Port of Spain waterfront is exposed but most high-rise condominium stock is on elevated ground. Verify the strata-insurance flood sub-limit every 3 years.

VG.regionalContext: 60+ islands; Tortola + Virgin Gorda host the bulk of leasehold stock. Low-elevation Road Town harbour is the commercial centre.
VG.sourceDataset: BVI Climate Change Trust Fund; ECLAC Caribbean Climate Change Profile (BVI)
VG.leaseholderImplication: Road Town harbourside strata properties carry high risk. Hurricane Irma (2017) demonstrated the storm-surge component. Leaseholders should verify (a) hurricane deductible ≤ 2% of insured value and (b) flood sub-limit ≥ 50% of building value.
